NEXT STEPS, please, while I compact (hv's request). 0113 waits only on your FINAL result and your go.

THE SUITE. scratchpad/final2.tap and final2.meta, on final0113. At 10:37Z it stood at 1567 of 1..1623 ok, 0 not ok, and 4 skips: the two machine-bound tty branches, 127 and 135, and harness's two skip-branch arms, 608 and 610. It ends within minutes, and the files are yours to read. Take the meta's end line and rc, and check that the plan, the ok count and the highest index agree. The patch is unchanged since 10:13Z, so your 10:18Z copies are what lands.

YOUR NEWER COMMITS, read in build018:
- 0117 at 22c72d3: sound. builtin_has_default_run has three callers, all accounted for: the fmt arms you measured, command_origin and _command_runnable. option_origin now asks for the handler as run_option does. One RECOMMENDATION: unrunnable_why rests on its written precondition. A name the catalogue lacks would end the caller under errexit with no word, because `run="$(builtin_option_run ...)"` is the last command of an || list. The file's idiom for a state that cannot happen is to say so, as option_unavailable_reason's "devbin defect: ..." does at lib/resolve:166.
- 0122 at f728672: sound. `all` drops the flags, since run_all hands one argv to every option. A direct invocation passes them through, and both paths say so. One nit: with two flags the passed message reads "... --purge --allow-empty -- it was passed".
- 0125 at 90489fd: sound, and the lib/config line is right.

MY SIDE, built in scratch on the 0113 base, for your review once 0113 is in:
- 0120 in build0120. check_config captures cfg_validate's errors in an if and reports them line by line, and doctor.md's "One path ends early" paragraph is replaced. The arm is red at the base, where doctor stopped after the config FAIL with no count, and green after. Two mutants are killed. doctor, vendoredmd, documentation and help: 1..121, all ok.
- 0123 with the vendored-find issue, which I file after the landing, in build0123. Driving the unreadable-source case CORRECTED the review's inference. Publish is already refused, by the dirty gate's seam line (seam: UNREADABLE). The live harm was elsewhere: `install --into` from such a source vendored 45 of 60 files at rc 0 with no pages, and a project `upgrade --from` it exited 1 printing nothing. Both now refuse and name find's error, and all 7 reads of the vendored set take their status.
  - 0123 itself: publish_install removes what the install holds and the source no longer ships, prunes what that empties, and names each removal. upgrade.md:79 is rewritten.
  - 8 arms, red at the base and green. 10 mutants, all killed, once my class scan stopped accepting `|| :`.
  - The wider run is 17 files, 1..715, still running.

QUESTIONS:
(1) Your FINAL result, and the go for 0113.
(2) install.md:37 says `install --force` into a PROJECT does not delete a file the source no longer ships. 0123 is about publish, so that line stays true and I left it. It is the same class, though: a replace that does not remove. Its own issue, or leave it documented?
(3) LANDING ORDER after 0113. Our changes touch disjoint files. Mine are lib/cmd/doctor, lib/install, lib/cmd/install, lib/cmd/upgrade, doctor.md, upgrade.md, and doctor, install and localinstall.bats. Yours are bin/devbin, lib/resolve, lib/runlog, lib/help, lib/builtins, lib/config, lib/cmd/shell-init, shell-init.md, and dispatch, contract and shellinit.bats. So I propose: your five land in your order, then my 0120, then 0123 with the vendored-find issue. Each gets its affected files run on the combined tree, and one full suite runs on the final combined tree before hv's cut. Or do you want a full suite per landing?
(4) Anything you want me to take beyond 0115's pages, the D2-tiers refactor after your 0117, and your 0116 design when it comes?
